theory.intro: The bases are non-zero and the indices are integers. The index laws work the same way when an index is negative: add when multiplying, subtract when dividing, multiply when raising a power to a power. At the end, rewrite any negative index as a reciprocal.
facts: $a^{m}\times a^{n}=a^{m+n}$, $a^{m}\div a^{n}=a^{m-n}$ and $\left(a^{m}\right)^{n}=a^{mn}$ all hold for $a\ne0$ and integer indices $m$ and $n$, including negative indices.
$a^{-n}=\frac{1}{a^{n}}$, so a result such as $x^{-4}$ is written $\frac{1}{x^{4}}$.
Handle the coefficients separately from the indices, multiplying or dividing them as ordinary numbers.
A coefficient only takes the index when it is **inside the brackets**: $3a^{-5}=\frac{3}{a^{5}}$ leaves the $3$, but $\left(4w^{-3}\right)^{2}=\frac{16}{w^{6}}$ squares the $4$.
steps: Apply any outside power to every factor inside the brackets, including the coefficient.
Apply the index law to each base, keeping the negative signs.
Rewrite any negative index as a reciprocal so the answer has positive indices.

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $x^{-4}\times x^{2}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $x\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Add the indices because the bases are the same.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}x^{-4}\times x^{2}\\&=x^{-4+2}\\&=x^{-2}\\&=\frac{1}{x^{2}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\frac{a^{-6}}{a^{-9}}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $a\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract the denominator's index. Subtracting a negative adds.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{a^{-6}}{a^{-9}}\\&=a^{-6-(-9)}\\&=a^{3}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\left(y^{-4}\right)^{3}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $y\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply the indices, then rewrite the negative index as a reciprocal.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\left(y^{-4}\right)^{3}\\&=y^{-4\times3}\\&=y^{-12}\\&=\frac{1}{y^{12}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\left(h^{-3}\right)^{-2}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $h\ne0$.
Simplify $4m^{-3}\times(-3m^{-2})$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $m\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply the coefficients and add the indices separately.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4m^{-3}\times(-3m^{-2})\\&=-12m^{-3+(-2)}\\&=-12m^{-5}\\&=-\frac{12}{m^{5}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\frac{15d^{-2}}{6d^{-5}}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $d\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Divide the coefficients and subtract the indices separately.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{15d^{-2}}{6d^{-5}}\\&=\frac{5}{2}d^{-2-(-5)}\\&=\frac{5}{2}d^{3}\\&=\frac{5d^{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\left(4t^{-3}\right)^{2}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $t\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The coefficient is inside the brackets, so it is squared too.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\left(4t^{-3}\right)^{2}\\&=4^{2}t^{-3\times2}\\&=16t^{-6}\\&=\frac{16}{t^{6}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\left(3c^{-2}\right)^{-3}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $c\ne0$.
Simplify $7\left(d^{-3}\right)^{2}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $d\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The power applies only to the factor inside the brackets.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}7\left(d^{-3}\right)^{2}\\&=7d^{-3\times2}\\&=7d^{-6}\\&=\frac{7}{d^{6}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\frac{20p^{-2}q^{3}}{5p^{2}q^{-4}}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $p,q\ne0$.
Simplify $3y^{-4}\times 6xy^{5}\div 2xy^{-2}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $x,y\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply and divide from left to right, applying the laws to each base separately.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3y^{-4}\times 6xy^{5}\div 2xy^{-2}\\&=9x^{1-1}y^{-4+5-(-2)}\\&=9x^{0}y^{3}\\&=9y^{3}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $\left(3m^{2}n^{-2}\right)^{-2}\times 6\left(m^{-1}n^{3}\right)^{2}$, writing your answer with positive indices. Assume $m,n\ne0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Apply each bracket power first, then multiply the coefficients and combine matching bases.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\left(3m^{2}n^{-2}\right)^{-2}\times 6\left(m^{-1}n^{3}\right)^{2}\\&=\frac{1}{9}m^{-4}n^{4}\times 6m^{-2}n^{6}\\&=\frac{2}{3}m^{-4+(-2)}n^{4+6}\\&=\frac{2}{3}m^{-6}n^{10}\\&=\frac{2n^{10}}{3m^{6}}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Find the value of $n$ that makes $\frac{x^{-5}}{x^{n}}=x^{2}$ true for every non-zero value of $x$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The division law gives $x^{-5-n}=x^{2}$. For the identity to hold for every non-zero $x$, the indices must agree.
$\begin{aligned}-5-n&=2\\-n&=7\\n&=-7\end{aligned}$
